newsitem.title: CHILE: Motorola sees 1997 Latam sales up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees 1997 Latam sales up sharply.

text.p: U.S. telecom equipment maker Motorola expects to report sales this year in Latin America 30 percent higher than the $1.3 billion posted in 1996, said Paul Velasco, general manager of Motorola Chile.
Strongest growth is seen in the Mexican and Brazilian markets which already account for around half of the company's sales in the region, Velasco told a news conference.
Velasco declined to give details of sales by country or by product.

In Chile, the company is studying whether to sell its stake in telecom Entel's personal telephone division following Entel's decision to use rival Ericsson technology instead of Motorola for its new mobile telephone network, he said.
"Under the shareholder's agreement, Motorola has flexible options to buy or sell its participation in Entel Telefonia Personal," said Velasco.
"We are studying the different possibilities and should have a decision within four weeks."
Motorola owns 40 percent of Entel Telefonia Personal.
Entel, Chile's largest long-distance carrier, announced last week that it had clinched a $106 million deal with Swedish firm Ericsson for the mobile network.
